title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 66-67). U is a smooth variety over a field K. X is a 'complexification', i.e. a compactification with normal-crossings boundary D = X \ U = ∪ D_i. For a subset J, D_J = ∩_{j∈J} D_j is the stratum. X_J is the étale/henselian localization of X along D_J, and U_J = X_J ∩ U is the trace of U, morally the punctured tubular neighbourhood of the stratum. E_U, E_{U_J}, E_{D_J} denote 'arithmetic' fundamental groups, i.e. extensions of Gal(K̄/K). T^J ≅ Ẑ(1)^J is the tame inertia, i.e. π1 of the fibre (Ḡ_m)^J. Base points are fixed via a universal pro-covering of D_J and an embedding of the function field L̃_J into L̄.

The sequence (37), T^J → E_{U_J} → E_{D_J} → 1, is then defined. Homotopically, U_J is (up to homotopy equivalence) the total space of a bundle over D_J whose fibre is a product of punctured discs, ≃ (S^1)^J.

Grothendieck worries that the sequence is not left exact. The long exact homotopy sequence contains a boundary map π2(D_J) → π1(fibre) = T^J. This map is given by the first Chern classes of the normal line bundles O(D_j)|_{D_J} evaluated on spherical classes.

He argues as follows. The 'inclusion' U_J → U and the structure maps give a commutative square:
- U_J → X_J (which is homotopy equivalent to D_J),
- U → Spec K = ξ,
- X_J → ξ.
This yields a morphism of homotopy exact sequences:
- top: π2(X_J) = π2(D_J) → π1(Ḡ_m^J) = T^J → π1(U_J) = E_{U_J} → π1(X_J) = E_{D_J} → 1;
- bottom: π2(ξ) = 0 → π1(U_ξ̄) = π_{U/K} → π1(U) = E_U → E_K → 1.

Since π2(ξ) = 0, the composite π2(D_J) → T^J → π_{U/K} vanishes. So if T^J → π_{U/K} (inertia into the geometric fundamental group) is injective, the boundary map π2(D_J) → T^J is zero. Then (37) becomes a genuine extension 1 → T^J → E_{U_J} → E_{D_J} → 1, mapping to 1 → π_{U/K} → E_U → E_K → 1; this is diagram (38) on the next page.

Purpose: in the Longue Marche programme, to describe the inertia ('multiplicative type') subgroups T^J ⊂ π_{U/K} attached to boundary strata. These are defined up to conjugacy, one class for each point of D_J. They are the higher-dimensional analogue of cusp inertia and of 'tangential base points' at strata, e.g. Dehn-twist subgroups for M_{g,n}.
errors: The deduction itself is valid. But the premise 'sachant que T^J → π_{U/K} est injectif' is false in general and must be a standing (anabelian / 'good' situation) hypothesis.
Counterexample 1: U = A^1 ⊂ P^1 has trivial π1, so the inertia Ẑ(1) maps to 1.

Counterexample 2: U = P^2 minus a point, compactified by blowing up. The exceptional divisor E ≅ P^1 has normal bundle O(-1). U_J is homotopic to S^3 (the Hopf bundle), so π2(E) = Z → Z is an isomorphism and T → π1(U_J) is zero. Hence (37) is genuinely not left exact in general, and Grothendieck's worry ('zizanie') is justified.
On p. 67 he simply 'admits' left exactness. This is fine for hyperbolic curves and for M_{g,n}-type situations, where Dehn-twist subgroups are free abelian of rank |J|.

Minor gap: π2 should be understood geometrically / étale-homotopically, with D_J taken over K̄ and component by component. The maps T^J → π_{U/K} are only defined up to inner automorphisms; he acknowledges both points on p. 67.

ideas.what: Punctured étale tubular neighbourhood U_J of a normal-crossing stratum D_J. Its fundamental group is an extension of π1(D_J) by the tame inertia Ẑ(1)^J, with U_J homotopically a (punctured-disc)^J bundle over D_J.
ideas.modern_name: Log fundamental group of a log stratum / tame fundamental group of a henselian tubular neighbourhood; Abhyankar's lemma; Kato–Nakayama space
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA1 Exp. XIII (Grothendieck–Murre tame fundamental group, 1971 Springer LNM 208); log geometry (Fontaine–Illusie, K. Kato, Kato–Nakayama, Vidal, Hoshi)

ideas.what: Boundary map π2(D_J) → Ẑ(1)^J (Chern classes of normal bundles) as the obstruction to left exactness. It is killed by comparison with U → Spec K whenever inertia injects into the geometric π1.
ideas.modern_name: Euler class / Gysin boundary of the normal circle bundle; injectivity of inertia (anabelian 'good' strata)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical topology; inertia injectivity results by Nakamura, Mochizuki, Hoshi–Mochizuki for curves and configuration spaces
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Dehn-twist/inertia subgroups for M_{g,n} informally

ideas.what: Comparison of the homotopy exact sequences of U_J → X_J and U → Spec K, giving the diagram of extensions of E_{D_J} and E_K (inertia 'multiplicative types' T^J → π_{U/K}, defined up to conjugacy, one class for each point of D_J).
ideas.modern_name: Inertia subgroups at boundary strata / tangential base points for higher-dimensional varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989), Ihara–Nakamura (Dehn twists, M_{g,n}), Mochizuki

missed.claim: An explicit remark that injectivity of inertia T^J ↪ π_{U/K} forces the vanishing of the normal-bundle Chern-class boundary π2(D_J) → Ẑ(1)^J. It is a simple, correct observation, but a nice homotopy-theoretic criterion that does not seem to be stated in this form in Grothendieck's published texts.
missed.quote: qui montre que le composé π2(D_J) → T^J → π_{U/K} est nul — donc sachant que T^J → π_{U/K} est injectif, on conclurait que π2(D_J) → T^J est nul !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a necessary condition (vanishing of c1(N_{D_j}) on spherical classes of strata) for a normal-crossings compactification to have 'anabelian' inertia. This is mildly relevant to higher-dimensional anabelian geometry and log configuration spaces, but is easy and implicitly known.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard homotopy-theoretic argument about inertia at normal-crossing strata. It is correct conditional on an injectivity hypothesis that fails in general. The content is close to known tame/log fundamental group theory and folklore about Dehn-twist subgroups; it is historically interesting as a working sketch of the higher-dimensional Longue Marche, but not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'C'est par cela que (3) est défini' should read '(37)', as referenced on p. 67.
The insertion above 'la fibré' reads approximately 'défini à l'équivalence d'homotopie près' and qualifies 'la fibre, morale, d'un produit de disques sur D_J'.
The garbled '$\frac{1}{1}J$ [?]' above π1(Ḡ_m^J) is 'T^J' with '≅' beneath it; the adjacent word is likely 'seconde'/'secante' and is uncertain.
Labels below the bottom row are π_{U/K} under π1(U_ξ̄), E_U under π1(U), and E_K under π1(ξ). Labels above the top row are E_{U_J} and E_{D_J}.
The inserted note '(le composé)' sits above 'π2(D_J) → T^J → π_{U/K} est nul'.
The vertical arrow X_J ← D_J is labelled 'équivalence d'homotopie'; the arrow U_J → X_J may carry a small label (possibly 'i').
